Commentary.Commentary: We are back. Sediqullah Atal and Abdul Malik to open for Afghanistan. Richard Ngarava to bowl first.
...THE CHASE...

Afghanistan will be delighted for the way they have performed with the ball. It was a professional performance yet again. Despite resting Fazalhaq Farooqi and Naveed Zadran, Azmatullah Omarzai bowled well with the new ball. However, as said earlier, it was the spin duo who troubled the hosts and as things stand, it is Afghanistan who are on top and could well clean sweep the series. Can Zimbabwe pull off something? Stay tuned.

Well, that was another abysmal batting performance Zimbabwe. They have struggled once again! Once, Afghanistan chose to bowl first, the pressure was on Zimbabwe right from the start knowing their batting performance. They started to crumble against AM Ghazanfar and Rashid Khan who overall took 8 wickets with the former registering a five fer. Sean Williams showed a lot of character for his fifty but still, overall, it was a struggle once again.

Zimbabwe (Playing XI) - Joylord Gumbie, Ben Curran, Craig Ervine (C), Sean Williams, Sikandar Raza, Brian Bennett, Tadiwanashe Marumani (WK), Wellington Masakadza, Newman Nyamhuri, Richard Ngarava, Trevor Gwandu.

Afghanistan (Playing XI) -  Sediqullah Atal, Abdul Malik, Hashmatullah Shahidi (C), Rahmat Shah, Mohammad Nabi, Ikram Alikhil (WK), Azmatullah Omarzai, Rashid Khan, AM Ghazanfar, Fareed Ahmad, Bilal Sami.
TOSS - Afghanistan have opted to BOWL first!

The hosts were demolished in the second game! They got a real beating from a rampant Afghanistan side. This is now a must win game for the hosts if they want to avoid a series defeat. However, Afghanistan will be high on confidence and will want to repeat their performance from the first game! They are favourites to come out victorious again but Zimbabwe are a side who can't be taken lightly.
... MATCH DAY ...

Afghanistan heads into the final ODI against Zimbabwe with an unassailable lead in the series. After dominating the preceding T20I series, they've maintained their impressive form in the ODI format. While rain washed out the opening ODI, Afghanistan showcased their superiority with a convincing victory in the second match. Even if Zimbabwe manages to win this final encounter, the best they can achieve is a shared series, as Afghanistan has already secured at least a piece of the trophy. The match represents not just the ODI series finale at Harare, but also marks the conclusion of Afghanistan's successful white-ball tour of Zimbabwe before the two sides don the whites. So what has been the problem with Zimbabwe? Batting? Bowling? Both, in all fairness. Zimbabwe's performance has been concerning across all departments. Their batting lineup has been particularly troublesome, with both established stars and newcomers failing to make their mark. The top order's inability to provide solid starts has been compounded by an underperforming middle order, where veterans Craig Ervine, Sean Williams, and Sikandar Raza – typically the backbone of Zimbabwe's batting – have been notably quiet. The team's batting woes were starkly evident in the first ODI, where they crumbled to 44-5 before rain provided a reprieve. The bowling unit hasn't fared much better. Front-line pacers Richard Ngarava and Blessing Muzarabani, usually reliable wicket-takers, have struggled to make early breakthroughs or maintain pressure. To salvage their pride and end the series on a positive note, Zimbabwe will need to address these multiple areas of concern and mount a strong performance. Afghanistan has been equally opposite in all facets of the game. The batting lineup has been impressive, with young Sediqullah Atal announcing his arrival on the international stage in style, already notching up a century. The top order's solidity has been further reinforced by Abdul Malik who has displayed promise, while captain Hashmatullah Shahidi has anchored the middle order with reliable performances. The bowling unit has been equally effective, with different players stepping up at crucial moments. AM Ghazanfar has been the standout performer, claiming four wickets in the series and demonstrating remarkable control. The pace department has complemented the spin attack effectively, maintaining pressure throughout the innings. What makes their bowling performance even more remarkable is that they've achieved this dominance without a single over from their star bowler Rashid Khan which indeed is a testament to the team's growing depth and versatility in the bowling department. Can the Afghans clinch the series on the back of these strong performances, or will Zimbabwe salvage some pride and finish the series on a positive note?
